text:
Recent research supports evaluating explanations beyond textual similarity. [Shimizu et al. (2024/WWW 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13248) show that conventional explanation scores can miss alignment with users’ positive and negative opinions; their review-derived evidence is unavailable here, so sentiments require explicitly supplied feedback. [ALERT (NAACL 2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.137/) evaluates explanations using purchase histories and reports 70% concordance with expert judgments. Its annotation study reports Krippendorff’s α=0.24—a caution against treating subjective judgments as reliable ground truth. A [2024 recommendation study](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10664-024-10483-3) separately measures relevance and redundancy, recognizing that a correct recommendation may still be unnecessary.

A practical synthesis—not an established four-class standard—is to annotate separate dimensions: broad similarity (shared documented attributes), complementarity (distinct function supporting an evidenced purpose), functional overlap (same documented function), and identification/evidence sufficiency. Reserve “useful” and “unnecessary” judgments for supported intent or explicit feedback; overlap alone does not establish redundancy. Record item/history identifiers, exact supporting title/description or feedback spans, rationale, and an unknown option. Interaction histories and timestamps do not establish ownership, compatibility, satisfied needs, or simulator traits.

For calibration, independently double-annotate a pilot before showing model explanations; revise ambiguous examples, preserve original disagreements, and report per-dimension agreement, label frequencies, abstention rates, and adjudication outcomes. [CHI 2025 research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3706598.3714319) warns that LLM explanations can anchor annotators and increase agreement without establishing correctness. [GRACE (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04525), although about grounded question answering, offers a transferable sequence: assess evidence sufficiency, extract support, then answer or abstain. Unidentified items should trigger abstention, not speculative complaints.
